issue: Does the term "controlled substance" in U.S.S.G. § 4B1.2(b) have a uniform federal meaning, or does its meaning vary according to the state of conviction?

sides.position: "Controlled substance" in § 4B1.2(b) varies with the state of conviction, so a state drug conviction counts under the Guidelines if it fits that state's definition, read by plain language.
cases: United States v. Jones, 15 F.4th 1288 (10th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Jones, 32 F.4th 1290 (10th Cir. 2022)

sides.position: "Controlled substance" in § 4B1.2(b) has a uniform federal definition, consistent with the categorical approach and Taylor's national-uniformity principle.
cases: United States v. Jones, 32 F.4th 1290 (10th Cir. 2022) (Tymkovich, C.J., dissenting from denial of rehearing en banc)

this_court: Adopts the state-of-conviction position in the panel decision, which the court declined to revisit en banc
quote: Our sister circuits are sharply divided on the question presented in Jones and the correct approach to answering it.
cite: United States v. Jones, 32 F.4th 1290 (10th Cir. 2022)
